content: Do not take quinapril if you are pregnant. If you become pregnant while taking quinapril, contact your doctor immediately, as this medication may harm the fetus. Quinapril is prescribed to treat high blood pressure, either alone or in combination with other medications. It is also used in combination with other medications to manage heart failure. Quinapril belongs to a class of drugs known as angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors. It works by reducing certain chemicals that tighten blood vessels, allowing blood to flow more smoothly and enabling the heart to pump blood more efficiently. Quinapril is available as an oral tablet and is typically taken once or twice daily. To ensure consistent use, take it at the same time(s) each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take quinapril exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it, or take it more frequently than prescribed. Your doctor will likely start you on a low dose and gradually increase it, usually no more than once every one or two weeks. Quinapril helps control high blood pressure and heart failure but does not cure these conditions. Continue taking quinapril even if you feel well, and do not stop taking it without consulting your doctor. Quinapril may be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before taking quinapril, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to quinapril or any other ACE inhibitors, such as benazepril, captopril, enalapril, fosinopril, lisinopril, moexipril, perindopril, ramipril, or trandolapril. Also, inform them about all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, nutritional supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Be sure to mention diuretics (water pills), lithium, potassium supplements, and tetracycline. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you closely for side effects. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had heart, liver, or kidney disease; lupus; scleroderma; diabetes; or angioedema, a condition causing difficulty swallowing or breathing and painful swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs. Let your doctor know if you are planning to become pregnant or are breastfeeding. If you are undergoing surgery, including dental surgery, inform your doctor or dentist that you are taking quinapril. Be aware that diarrhea, vomiting, inadequate fluid intake, or excessive sweating can lead to a drop in blood pressure, causing lightheadedness or fainting. Consult your doctor before using salt substitutes containing potassium. If your doctor prescribes a low-salt or low-sodium diet, follow these instructions carefully. If you miss a dose of quinapril, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to make up for a missed one. Quinapril may cause side effects. Inform your doctor if you experience dizziness, excessive tiredness, cough, upset stomach, or vomiting, especially if these symptoms are severe or persistent. Some side effects can be serious. Contact your doctor immediately if you experience swelling of the face, throat, tongue, lips, eyes, hands, feet, ankles, or lower legs; hoarseness; difficulty breathing or swallowing; yellowing of the skin or eyes; fever, sore throat, chills, or other signs of infection; chest pain; lightheadedness; or fainting. If you experience any unusual problems while taking this medication, contact your doctor. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store quinapril in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excess heat and moisture (not in the bathroom). Dispose of outdated or unneeded medication properly. Consult your pharmacist about the correct disposal method. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call 911. Symptoms of overdose may include lightheadedness and fainting. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your blood pressure should be checked regularly to monitor your response to quinapril. Your doctor may order lab tests to evaluate your body’s response to the medication. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
